message.content:
**The Mom Test** is a customer interviewing methodology created by entrepreneur **Rob Fitzpatrick** and described in his 2013 book *The Mom Test: How to Talk to Customers & Learn If Your Business Is a Good Idea When Everyone Is Lying to You*. It's a framework for asking questions that elicit honest, actionable feedback—even from people who want to be nice to you, like your mom. ## The Core Concept The name comes from a thought experiment: if you ask your mom whether your business idea is good, she'll probably say yes—not because it actually is, but because she loves you and doesn't want to hurt your feelings. Most people do the same thing; they give polite, encouraging answers that lead to **false validation**. The Mom Test solves this by teaching you to ask questions in a way that **even your mom couldn't lie to you**. ## The 3 Rules The entire framework boils down to three principles: | Rule | What It Means | Example | |------|-------------|---------| | **1. Talk about their life, not your idea** | Don't pitch your product. Don't describe what you're building. Ask about their actual experiences. | ❌ "Would you use a meal-planning app?"
✅ "Walk me through how you planned dinner last week." | | **2. Ask about specifics in the past, not generics in the future** | Past behavior is data; future intentions are fiction. | ❌ "Would you pay for this?"
✅ "The last time you faced this problem, what did you do?" | | **3. Talk less and listen more** | The more you talk about your idea, the more you bias their responses. Ask, then shut up. | Let silence work for you—some of the best answers come after an awkward pause. | ## Why It Matters Most startups fail because they build something nobody wants. The biggest trap is asking **bad questions that lead to misleading answers**—compliments, hypothetical fluff, and wishlists. The Mom Test helps you uncover: - Real problems people actually have - How they're currently solving those problems (workarounds, hacks, existing solutions) - Whether they're already spending money or time to fix the issue - Emotional signals (frustration, excitement) that reveal true priorities ## What to Ask vs. What to Avoid | ✅ Ask About | ❌ Avoid | |-------------|----------| | Current pain points and frustrations | "Do you think this is a good idea?" | | Past behavior and specific experiences | "Would you use this if it existed?" | | Current solutions and workarounds | Leading questions that fish for approval | | Spending habits and budget | Hypothetical future behavior | | How they discovered existing tools | Feature requests from people who haven't committed | ## Key Takeaways - **Commitment beats compliments**—a "sounds great!" means nothing; someone scheduling a follow-up or pre-paying means everything - **20–30 conversations** are needed before patterns emerge (5 interviews just gives you anecdotes) - **The Mom Test is a mindset, not a script**—it's about recognizing in real-time when a conversation drifts into hypotheticals and steering it back to concrete facts The book is widely recommended in startup and product management circles as one of the most practical, actionable guides for customer discovery and validating business ideas. --- Sources: 1. https://gonogo.team/the-mom-test 2. https://tldv.io/blog/the-mom-test/ 3. https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mom-test 4. https://www.dictionary.com/browse/mom-test 5. https://blog.uxtweak.com/the-mom-test/ 6. https://readingraphics.com/book-summary-the-mom-test/ 7. https://sciencepark.se/en/article/the-mom-test-how-to-get-others-to-share-what-they-really-think-about-your-idea/ 8. https://www.francescacortesi.com/blog/9zu6w6hj7y4z8zft524e5ouc734pjp 9. https://nightingaledesignresearch.com/insights/book-review-the-mom-test-by-rob-fitzpatrick/ 10. https://hellopm.co/word/moms-test/ 11. https://inkubator.si/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/The-Mom-Test-by-@robfitz.pdf 12. https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/book-review-mom-test-rob-fitzpatrick-jagbir-singh-lehl-0ftgc 13. https://www.momtestbook.com/ 14. https://www.maxmednik.com/blog/notes-on-the-mom-test-by-rob-fitzpatrick
